subject: Shadow Evals: retention/redaction + SOC 2 evidence request (Bluefin Bank)
related_links: Google Drive: Security Review Packet (internal link)
body:
From: Ava Patel <ava.patel@bluefinbank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@bluefinbank.com>, security-team@bluefinbank.com
Date: Mon, Nov 10, 2025 at 9:14 AM
Subject: Shadow Evals: retention/redaction + SOC 2 evidence request

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Before we can approve enabling “Shadow Evals” in our Redwood environment, our security/GRC team needs clarification on data handling and auditability.

Can you confirm:
1) What parts of the request/response are retained for shadow evaluations (prompts, completions, tool calls, metadata)?
2) Default retention periods, and whether we can configure them (including “metrics only”).
3) Redaction: what is redacted by default, and can we provide custom patterns (account numbers, names, etc.)?
4) Residency: we run us-east only. Does shadow execution or logging ever leave our region?
5) Audit logs: do you log admin actions (enable shadowing, sampling % changes, retention changes)? Can you provide sample events?
6) Compliance: can you share your latest SOC 2 Type II and subprocessor list?

If there’s a standard “security packet” for this feature, that’s fine too.

Best,
Ava Patel
Security Engineering
Bluefin Bank


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Patel <ava.patel@bluefinbank.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@bluefinbank.com>, security-team@bluefinbank.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Nov 10, 2025 at 11:02 AM
Subject: Re: Shadow Evals: retention/redaction + SOC 2 evidence request

Hi Ava,

Absolutely — below are direct answers, and I’m attaching our current “Shadow Evals Data Retention & Redaction Overview” plus SOC 2 and subprocessors.

1) What is retained
Shadow Evals has two distinct data surfaces:
- (A) Derived evaluation metrics (always on when shadowing is enabled): latency/cost deltas, outcome labels, and aggregate scores.
- (B) Payload samples (optional; controlled): limited prompt/output snippets to support debugging and judge calibration.

By default for beta we retain (A) only.

For (A) metrics, we store:
- Request metadata needed to join primary and shadow runs: request_id, route, model target identifier, region, timestamp, sampling policy id, and high-level status.
- Performance: end-to-end latency, queue delay (shadow only), tokens in/out (binned), and estimated cost.
- Quality: format adherence result, safety policy outcomes (pass/fail categories), and judge score summaries.

We do NOT store full prompts/completions by default.

2) Retention (defaults + configurability)
- Metrics (A): default 30 days (configurable; we can support 7/30/90 for the beta accounts we’re onboarding).
- Payload samples (B): default OFF. If enabled, default 7 days, and restricted-access only.
- “Metrics only” mode: yes (that is the default).

3) Redaction
- Payload samples (B) are redacted before persistence using our standard PII filters (emails, phone numbers, SSNs, IPs, common identifiers) plus configurable allow/deny lists.
- For custom patterns: yes, you can provide regex-based patterns (e.g., your account number formats). Those are applied before storage.
- For metrics (A), we avoid free-form tags; fields are enumerated/bucketed to prevent accidental leakage.

4) Residency
If your traffic is pinned to us-east, shadow execution and telemetry ingestion remain in that region. Shadow is executed asynchronously, but it is not replayed cross-region.

5) Audit logs
Yes — we audit administrative changes related to shadowing: enable/disable, sampling %, target changes, retention settings, and access grants to payload samples.
I’ve attached a sample event schema.

6) Compliance packet
Attached:
- SOC 2 Type II (FY2025)
- Current subprocessor list

Two notes for clarity:
- Shadow Evals never blocks or modifies the primary response. If shadow fails, it fails “closed” and only impacts shadow metrics.
- For Bluefin, we can keep you in “metrics only” and still provide rollout gating signals (judge win-rate deltas, safety deltas, format adherence) without storing payload content.

If you’d like, we can do a 30-min working session where Marcus (Security Eng) walks through the audit log surface + how redaction is applied.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Product Lead
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Redwood_Inference_SOC2_TypeII_FY2025.pdf
- Subprocessors_List_2025-10-01.pdf
- Shadow_Evals_Data_Retention_and_Redaction_Overview_v0.9.pdf
- Redwood_Audit_Log_Event_Schema_Sample.json

From: Mark Chen <mark.chen@bluefinbank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Patel <ava.patel@bluefinbank.com>, security-team@bluefinbank.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Nov 11, 2025 at 8:27 AM
Subject: Re: Shadow Evals: retention/redaction + SOC 2 evidence request

Naomi,

Thanks — this is helpful.

A few follow-ups from GRC:

1) In “metrics only,” do you still transmit the prompt/completion to the shadow target at runtime (even if you don’t store it)? If so, how do you ensure it doesn’t end up in standard application logs?

2) For payload samples (if ever enabled), who at Redwood can access them? Is access time-bound / approval-based, and is it audited?

3) For judge scoring, are you using a third-party model API that could receive our content? Or is judge scoring internal to Redwood? (We may need to update our vendor inventory depending on the answer.)

4) Do the audit logs include reads (e.g., viewing payload samples), or only writes/changes?

Regards,
Mark Chen
GRC / Third-Party Risk
Bluefin Bank

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Mark Chen <mark.chen@bluefinbank.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ava Patel <ava.patel@bluefinbank.com>, security-team@bluefinbank.com
Date: Tue, Nov 11, 2025 at 10:05 AM
Subject: Re: Shadow Evals: retention/redaction + SOC 2 evidence request

Mark (and Ava),

Jumping in on the technical/security controls.

1) Runtime handling vs storage (“metrics only”)
Correct: the shadow target necessarily receives the same request payload at runtime in order to produce a shadow output for scoring. The control is that:
- Shadow execution is isolated from the primary path and uses a separate worker/queue.
- We explicitly disable request/response body logging for shadow runs by default. Shadow worker logs include request_id and error codes only.
- Any optional payload sampling is a separate, gated feature (off by default) and uses a separate storage path with stricter ACLs.

2) Access controls for payload samples
If payload sampling is enabled:
- Access is restricted to a small, named group in Security/Compliance + on-call SRE (break-glass) with manager approval.
- Access is time-bound (expiring grants) and tied to a ticket (we typically reference an internal INT-* request).
- All accesses are audited (including view/export actions).

3) Judge scoring + third parties
Judge scoring runs on Redwood-managed inference. We do not send your data to a third-party LLM provider for judging.

(Separately: if a customer configures an external judge endpoint, that’s possible in theory, but not part of the beta scope and would be explicitly configured by the customer with clear warnings and routing controls.)

4) Audit logs: reads and writes
We log both:
- Write events: config changes, enable/disable shadowing, sampling %, retention settings, target updates.
- Read/access events: viewing payload samples, exporting samples, and permission grants.

If helpful, we can provide a redacted set of example audit log events (create policy, enable sampling, view sample) showing actor, timestamp, source IP, and object identifiers.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Security Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Ava Patel <ava.patel@bluefinbank.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@bluefinbank.com>, security-team@bluefinbank.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 12, 2025 at 1:46 PM
Subject: Re: Shadow Evals: retention/redaction + SOC 2 evidence request

Naomi/Macus,

This addresses the main concerns.

Two last items before we submit for approval:

- Can you confirm we can run Shadow Evals with payload samples permanently OFF (metrics only), and still use the “halt rollout on regression” gating? Our preference is not to store content.

- For us-east only, can you confirm the metrics store used for Shadow Evals is also us-east, including backups?

If yes, we can proceed with a limited beta: 0.5% sampling on a single route, business hours only, with a hard kill-switch.

Thanks,
Ava


---

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ava Patel <ava.patel@bluefinbank.com>
Cc: Mark Chen <mark.chen@bluefinbank.com>, security-team@bluefinbank.com, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Nov 12, 2025 at 4:38 PM
Subject: Re: Shadow Evals: retention/redaction + SOC 2 evidence request

Ava,

Confirmed on both points:

1) Metrics-only + rollout gating
Yes — payload samples can remain permanently OFF. Rollout gates are computed from derived metrics (judge score summaries, safety deltas, format adherence, and latency/cost deltas). The gating policy evaluates aggregates over a window; it does not require stored prompt/completion bodies.

2) us-east residency (including backups)
Yes — for your deployment pinned to us-east, Shadow Evals metrics are stored and backed up in us-east. We do not replicate the underlying metrics dataset cross-region for your account.

Your proposed beta scope (0.5% on one route, business hours, kill-switch) matches what we consider a safe starting point. Once you share the route ID and candidate shadow target, we’ll draft a configuration proposal for your review.

Best,
Naomi

—
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Product Lead
Redwood Inference
